review.title: Nhận xét bài viết trên lớp
paragraphs: It is argued that advertising yield notable economic advantages, whereas some individuals contend that it leads to dissatisfaction caused by fostering personal discontentment among these people. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

Some might argue that advertising bring undeniable economic benefits. Its creative content and appealing visual effects stimulate consumer demand and spending power. The rise in consumption encourage higher production levels, which subsequently lead to expanded job opportunities in sectors such as marketing, media and design. Furthermore, this sharply generates greater state revenue through taxation. For example, e-commerce platforms like Shopee or Lazada in Vietnam rely heavily on advertising campaigns to attract customers, boosting not only their sales but also the entire digital retail sector.

Others claim that advertising can have negative social impacts by constantly presenting ideal lifestyles, unrealistic beauty standards and luxury possessions, which can foster dissatisfaction among viewers. Young people in particular often feel pressure to purchase trendy clothes or the latest smartphones after seeing advertisements on TikTok or Facebook. This can lead to frustration when they cannot afford them. Furthermore, more advertising can encourage materialistic values because people may start to believe that having more expensive items means having a better life. In the long run, this may create a more money-driven society.
Overall, I believe that both views valid to some certain extents. Advertising contributes to social dissatisfaction, but play a crucial role in economic development.

paragraphs: Advertising may bring economic advantages, whereas it can also leave people dissatisfied with their lives. There are strong cases to be made for both sides of the argument.

On the one hand, supporters of advertising often point to the undeniable economic benefits it can bring. Creative content and appealing visual effects can stimulate consumer demand. Increased spending encourages producers to raise output, which creates employment opportunities and tax revenue. For example, Shopee and Lazada use campaigns to attract customers and expand digital retail. Furthermore, advertising provides direct work in marketing, media and design. This wider spending can also support suppliers, transport services and public finances. The example therefore shows how advertising affects more than one company.

Those on the other side of the debate, however, argue that advertising entails negative social consequences. Ideal lifestyles, unrealistic beauty standards and luxury possessions may foster dissatisfaction among viewers. Young people may feel pressure to purchase trendy clothes or the latest phones promoted on TikTok and Facebook. When they cannot afford these items, they may experience frustration. Repeated pressure may then strengthen materialistic values and create a money-driven society. For this reason, viewers may judge their own possessions against an unrealistic standard. The social cost can remain after a campaign has ended.
In conclusion, advertising can promote demand, employment and state revenue. At the same time, it may cause dissatisfaction and encourage materialistic values.

paragraphs: It is argued that the news media - have an excessive amount of influence over modern life, and this is phenomenon represents a negative trend. While I agree news media outlets exert an unprecedented level of sway over the public, I disagree that the news that is entirely a negative development, as its societal benefits are equally significant.

On the one hand, it is undeniable that the news media have come to dominate daily routines. Owing the widespread access to the smartphones and the Internet, the individuals can now follow current events instantaneously, regardless of time or location. Consequently, consuming news has seamlessly integrated into people’s everyday lives. Furthermore, driven by intense competition within the media industry, news agencies prioritize sensational breaking content. By employing dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals, news outlets amplify the impact of their reporting, effectively shaping public opinion and steering collective focus.

On the other hand, although this powerful influence can bring clear drawbacks, it also serves an indispensable purpose. On negative note, continuous exposure to a stream of distressing and exaggerated news can overwhelm individuals, causing unnecessary anxiety and feelings of helplessness, even in situations that do not affect them directly. However, news coverage plays a vital role in alerting the public about pressing social issues, such as rising crime rates, impending natural disasters, or political corruption. Being regularly updated allow citizens to remain well-informed, better prepared for potential threats, and equipped to manage risks in an increasingly complex world.

paragraphs: It is argued that the news media have an excessive amount of influence over modern life, and this phenomenon represents a negative trend. While I agree news media outlets exert an unprecedented level of sway over the public, I disagree that this is entirely a negative development, as its societal benefits are equally significant.

It is undeniable that the news media have come to dominate daily routines. Owing to the widespread access to smartphones and the Internet, individuals can now follow current events instantaneously, regardless of time or location. Consequently, consuming news has seamlessly integrated into people’s everyday lives. Furthermore, driven by intense competition within the media industry, news agencies prioritize sensational breaking content. By employing dramatic headlines and eye-catching visuals, news outlets amplify the impact of their reporting, effectively shaping public opinion and steering collective focus.

Although this powerful influence can bring clear drawbacks, it also serves an indispensable purpose. On a negative note, continuous exposure to a stream of distressing and exaggerated news can overwhelm individuals, causing unnecessary anxiety and feelings of helplessness, even in situations that do not affect them directly. However, news coverage plays a vital role in alerting the public about pressing social issues, such as rising crime rates, impending natural disasters, or political corruption. Being regularly updated allows citizens to remain well-informed, better prepared for potential threats, and equipped to manage risks in an increasingly complex world.

In conclusion, while the news media undoubtedly hold immense sway over public consciousness and can occasionally induce stress, I do not consider this to be a purely negative shift. The informative power of news remains essential for individual safety and social stability.

paragraphs: Opinions differ on whether academic rewards should be reserved exclusively for students with the highest achievement or bestowed upon those who demonstrate progress. While acknowledging the importance of rewarding top performers, I believe schools should recognize both outstanding results and personal improvement to foster an inclusive learning environment.

On the one hand, acknowledging students with the best academic results is entirely justified. Those who consistently top the class have diligently applied themselves to their studies, meaning they fully deserve praises and special privileges. Such recognition not only validates their hard work but also inspires other students to study harder to win similar rewards, ultimately propelling overall academic standards forward. Furthermore, this kind of competition mirrors almost every aspect of real life, where top achievers are primary recipients of success. Being exposed to this reality early helps students thrive in the face of fierce competition, equipping them with the resilience needed to succeed in their future careers.

On the other hand, rewarding students who show progress is equally vital. Naturally, only a small fraction of exceptionally talented students can secure top positions. If rewards are strictly limited to this group, average or struggling learners may feel that their efforts are futile because they can never surpass these naturally gifted individuals. Consequently, they become disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to learn. Conversely, emphasizing personal growth encourages every student to remain diligent, fostering an understanding that self-improvement is essential regardless of their current academic level. This mindset - a constant desire to outdo oneself - often proves far more beneficial to long-term personal development than merely striving to defeat others.

In conclusion, while celebrating top academic achievements maintains high educational standards, rewarding individual improvements ensures that no students feel left behind. Therefore, educational institutions ought to combine both reward systems to maximize motivation across the student body.

paragraphs: Opinions differ on whether academic rewards should be reserved exclusively for students with the highest achievement or bestowed upon those who demonstrate progress. While acknowledging the importance of rewarding top performers, I believe schools should recognize both outstanding results and personal improvement to foster an inclusive learning environment.

Admittedly, acknowledging students with the best academic results is entirely justified. One reason is that those who consistently top the class have diligently applied themselves to their studies, meaning they fully deserve praises and special privileges. Such recognition not only validates their hard work but also inspires other students to study harder to win similar rewards, ultimately propelling overall academic standards forward. Furthermore, this kind of competition mirrors almost every aspect of real life, where top achievers are often rewarded for strong performance. Being exposed to this reality early helps students thrive in the face of fierce competition, equipping them with the resilience needed to succeed in their future careers.

However, rewarding students who show progress is equally vital. First, only a small fraction of exceptionally talented students can secure top positions. If rewards are strictly limited to this group, average or struggling learners may feel that their efforts are futile. This is because they may feel unable to surpass these high-achieving students. Consequently, they become disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to learn. Conversely, emphasizing personal growth encourages every student to remain diligent, fostering an understanding that self-improvement is essential regardless of their current academic level. This mindset - a constant desire to outdo oneself - often proves far more beneficial to long-term personal development than merely striving to defeat others.

In conclusion, while celebrating top academic achievements maintains high educational standards, rewarding individual improvements ensures that no students feel left behind. Therefore, educational institutions ought to combine both reward systems to maximize motivation across the student body.
